conviction_note: Q2 itself looks fine (independent-jeweler dollar sales ran +12%/+18%/+10% across May/Jun/Jul, Signet's exact fiscal quarter), but the same monthly series rolled over hard in August to +5% with units -8% and the opening-price-point category -19% in units — and this stock moves on the guide, not the quarter, into a setup where a beat-and-raise is already loudly paid for (Citi opened a public upside catalyst watch, 25d skew is -13.5 vol points i.e. calls bid, consensus PT ~$112 vs $82 spot); I net the August demand pulse against two genuine unpriced tariff positives and land modestly negative and well inside the ~10% implied move.

findings.finding: Edge Retail Academy's US independent-jeweler panel shows the category decelerating sharply in August 2026 — gross sales +5% YoY (vs +18% in June and +10% in July), units -8%, average retail sale +14% — with the opening-price-point sterling silver / alternative metals category at -5% dollars and -19% units; August is month one of Signet's fiscal Q3 and the month the H2 guide has to be built on.
findings.why_not_priced: The Edge series is published in jewelry trade press (JCK, InStore, Edge's own blog) five days before the print and is not carried by any financial wire, terminal or aggregator; Signet has only ~3 EPS estimates on the tape, so there is no sell-side machine converting a trade-press monthly into a Q3 comp. If it were priced, the 25-delta skew would not be -13.46 vol points (calls bid over puts) and Citi would not have opened a public 'upside 30-day catalyst watch' on 2026-09-08 expecting a raise to the top end of the range. The same series was benign through the quarter itself (+12/+18/+10 in May/Jun/Jul), so this is specifically a forward-guide signal, not a restatement of the Q2 print. Note the level is not transferable — Edge ran +12% in April while Signet comped +1.8% in Q1 — the sequential shape is the signal, and it is a ~7pt one-month deceleration.
findings.independence: Two different sources point the same way on the value-end consumer: PROG Holdings' Q2 2026 call named jewelry as one of only two categories at Purchasing Power that failed to grow GMV year over year (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/07/prog-prg-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/), and Pandora's calendar-Q2 2026 report showed North America like-for-like negative with US sales only 'stable' (https://wwd.com/accessories-news/jewelry/pandora-q2-results-2026-guidance-raised-early-announcement-1239092531/). The May/June/July Edge readings come from the same source cluster as this finding and are deliberately folded into it rather than filed separately.

findings.finding: The 15% Section 122 global import surcharge that underpinned Signet's 'mid-teens effective tariff rate for the year' expired 12:01am on 2026-07-24 and was replaced the same minute by Section 301 forced-labor duties of 10%–12.5% on the 60 economies covering Signet's sourcing base — a 2.5–5 point step down on India, the country Signet named as its principal tariff exposure, four days before its quarter ended and seven weeks after the FY27 guide was set.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a macro trade-law event that lands in the index, not in SIG's relative price; converting it requires knowing the specific sentence in Signet's 2026-06-02 call ('mid-teens effective tariff rate for the year') and that the guide was built on the 15% Section 122 number. With three estimates on the tape there is no published model of Signet's tariff line to revise. If it were priced you would see a tariff-relief note among the handful of SIG previews; instead the only visible preview thesis is Citi's generic 'inline Q2, raise to the top end', which is about demand, not landed cost. Slow-burning: Signet's ~$2.0bn inventory against ~$4bn COGS means post-July-24 landings mostly hit Q4/Q1 P&L, which is why I size it small.
findings.independence: Jewelry-specific confirmation of the rates and effective date from National Jeweler (https://nationaljeweler.com/articles/15165-new-trump-tariffs-what-they-mean-for-jewelry), which puts India/China/Thailand/HK/UAE at 12.5% and Canada/Mexico/Pakistan/Sri Lanka/UK at 10% — note it disagrees with a 10% figure reported for India elsewhere, so I treat the step-down as 2.5–5 points rather than a point estimate. This finding and the refund finding below share the tariff theme but rest on different documents (a USTR action versus Signet's own disclosure); they should be collapsed to one residual if scored as a cluster.

findings.finding: Signet has filed IEEPA refund claims on most goods where it was importer of record and had received only 'a small amount' as of 2026-06-02, with management stating it is too early to quantify the amount or timing 'as well as how any proceeds may be used' — meaning the FY27 guide contains none of it, while CBP had already built out mass electronic IEEPA refunds covering ~82% of affected entries by April 2026, i.e. during Signet's Q2.
findings.why_not_priced: The item is knowably excluded from guidance by the company's own words, and it is unquantifiable from outside — which is exactly why no estimate carries it and why the wire preview cannot contain it. The 'how any proceeds may be used' phrasing is a buyback tell: Signet has $355m remaining on the 2017 authorisation after a $50m ASR on 2026-06-08 and had $602.8m cash / ~$1.7bn liquidity at Q1, against a $3.2bn market cap. If the market were carrying this, the stock would not be at 8x the midpoint of a $9.20–$11.00 FY27 EPS guide and the put/call open interest ratio would not be 3.27. Wide band because the refund may land as a Q3 event, be excluded from adjusted EPS, or be deferred into contested CIT proceedings.
findings.independence: The refund mechanism and its timing come from a different source entirely — Skadden's account of the post-Supreme-Court CBP refund process (https://www.skadden.com/insights/publications/2026/03/tariff-refund-mechanism-takes-shape) — and the buyback capacity from Signet's 2026-06-08 8-K item 8.01 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/832988/000083298826000161/sig-20260608.htm). Shares the tariff theme with the finding above; different documents.

searched_and_found_nothing: Cause of the -13.15% 20-day drawdown: no company news between 2026-08-12 (earnings date PR) and today; the fall ran 2026-08-06 ($93.88) to 2026-08-20 ($81.02) with no identifiable catalyst in any wire, filing or trade-press source

Insider signal: the nine Form 4s filed 2026-08-24 are director awards dated 08-21 and the 2026-09-01 filing is Julie Yoakum, code F, 2,645.98 shares withheld for tax at $82.36 — no open-market selling or buying

Quiet 8-Ks: the only 2026 items outside earnings are a Gennette board appointment (05-07), the $50m ASR (06-08), AGM results (06-30) and director Andre Branch's resignation with the standard no-disagreement language (07-02); nothing anomalous

The 2026-08-11 appointment of Jamie Cygielman (Zales+Banter) and Pam Cloud (Blue Nile) looked like forced turnover but is the continued build-out of the brand-president structure begun in July 2025 (Kay/Peoples, CMO, sourcing) rather than replacement of incumbents — dropped as a finding

Blue Nile / James Allen migration breakage: Trustpilot and ConsumerAffairs show delayed orders and incomplete inventory migration but no dated, measurable step-change in review volume or rating I could anchor, so it does not clear the evidence bar

Gold: peaked $5,595 on 2026-01-29, bottomed ~$3,943 on 2026-06-30, back to ~$4,435 by 2026-09-07 — real and relevant to the 'flat to slightly up' H2 merchandise margin guide, but gold is the most-watched price on earth and is priced by definition; not filed as a finding
Lab-grown deflation: wholesale LGD prices -13% YoY in Q2 2026 versus -14% in Q1, i.e. decelerating, so no incremental AUR shock
Company hiring page / WARN notices: no 2026 Ohio or Texas WARN filings for Signet or Sterling Jewelers found; the Akron reductions on record are from the earlier Grow Brand Love reorg

Sell-side and wire copy (consensus $1.69 vs $1.61 LY, Zacks cut to Hold 2026-08-26, UBS $122, Wells Fargo, consensus PT ~$112, Citi upside catalyst watch $120) — all read as what is already in the price, not as findings
baseline_tension: It cuts against the baseline: the option chain pays up for upside (25d skew -13.46 vol points), the sell side has a live published upside catalyst watch into the print, and six of Signet's last eight prints went up — while the one dataset that covers the month after the quarter says the US jewelry demand pulse halved in August, so the two tariff positives I found agree with the priced lean and only the demand finding is genuinely against it.
